title: Sunday · bad color · the alley, right
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: The fifth kept: the alley behind the tavern, and for the first time something is right — the rust on the tin. The rest is still wrong. The book keeps it for the one right thing.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the alley from the mouth. The tavern's wall, mud. The sky, mud. The garage door, mud.

image.prompt: over-wet watercolor, muddy early-digital scan, an alley behind a tavern painted in muddy over-wet grays and browns, no words

panels.name: Mud

panels.composition: Tier 2: the tin roof's edge. Rust. And the rust is right — the bloom of it, the orange into the gray, the first thing the color gets right.

image.prompt: over-wet watercolor, muddy early-digital scan, close on a corrugated tin roof edge where rust blooms orange into gray with unexpected accuracy, no words
image.notes: The one right thing on the page. Draw the rust well and everything else badly.

panels.name: Rust

panels.composition: Tier 3: the alley again. Still mud. But the reader has seen the rust and looks for it. Held.

image.prompt: over-wet watercolor, muddy early-digital scan, the same muddy alley with a small patch of accurate rust on a roof edge, no words

panels.name: Again
